## `yuzie`

```text
Usage: yuzie [options] [command]

Real-time, git-aware kanban for your team, in your terminal.

Options:
  --version                              print the version
  --json                                 machine-readable output; no colour, no spinners
  --board <slug>                         use this board instead of the one in .yuzie/config.json
  --no-color                             disable colour (NO_COLOR is honoured too)
  -q, --quiet                            print only errors
  -v, --verbose                          debug logging on stderr
  --offline                              do not contact the server
  -y, --yes                              assume yes; take defaults instead of asking
  --config <path>                        use this config file
  -h, --help                             show help

Commands:
  init [options]                         detect the repo, sign in, create or link a board, write config, install hooks
  login                                  sign in with a device code; the token goes to the OS keychain
  logout                                 revoke this machine’s token and forget it
  whoami                                 show who you are, which server, and which board
  doctor [options]                       check node, git, sign-in, server, hooks and cache
  config                                 read and change .yuzie/config.json
  claim [options] <id>                   assign to yourself, move to Doing, create and check out the branch (§9.3)
  start [options] <id>                   like claim, but only checks out a branch that already exists
  finish [options] <id>                  pre-flight checks, then move the card on for review (§9.4)
  branch [options] <id>                  print the branch for a card; --create checks it out, --link records one
  sync [options]                         push queued changes, pull the board, re-scan git, and report what happened
  anchor <id> <location>                 attach a code location (file:line or file:start-end) to a card
  open [options] <id>                    open the card’s code in $EDITOR, or its PR / branch / link in a browser
  commits <id>                           list the commits linked to a card
  hooks                                  manage the git hooks
  add [options] <title...>               create a card
  list|ls [options]                      list cards, most recently active first
  card <id>                              everything about one card
  move <id> <column>                     move a card; the column matches by prefix
  done <id>                              move a card to the final column
  assign [options] <id> [handles...]     assign people or agents
  comment [options] <id> [text...]       add a comment; `-` reads it from stdin
  edit <id>                              edit a card in $EDITOR as YAML front matter + markdown
  rm <id>                                delete a card (asks first; --yes to skip)
  watch <id>                             follow a card’s activity
  unwatch <id>                           stop following a card
  check [options] <id> <item> [text...]  toggle checklist item n, or `check <id> add <text>`
  label [options] <id> <labels...>       add labels; --rm to remove them
  due <id> <date...>                     set the due date (friday, +3d, 2026-10-02) or `none`
  priority <id> <priority>               set priority p0..p3, or `none`
  boards                                 list your boards
  columns                                list this board’s columns
  members                                who is on this board, with roles
  share                                  print how a teammate joins this board
  invite [options] <who>                 invite someone by email or @handle
  who                                    who is online, and what they are working on
  activity [options]                     what happened recently
  token                                  API tokens for CI, scripts and agents
  completion <shell>                     print shell completion for bash, zsh or fish (see `yuzie completion --help`)
  upgrade [options]                      install the latest yuzie, the way this one was installed
  mcp [options]                          serve the board to an AI agent over MCP (stdio)
  feed                                   stream the board’s events live, one per line (Ctrl-C to stop)
```

## `yuzie init`

```text
Usage: yuzie init [options]

detect the repo, sign in, create or link a board, write config, install hooks

Options:
  --no-hooks  do not install git hooks
  -h, --help  show help
```

## `yuzie doctor`

```text
Usage: yuzie doctor [options]

check node, git, sign-in, server, hooks and cache

Options:
  --bundle [file]  also write a redacted diagnostic bundle (versions, config,
                   last 200 log lines, git facts)
  -h, --help       show help
```

## `yuzie config`

```text
Usage: yuzie config [options] [command]

read and change .yuzie/config.json

Options:
  -h, --help                   show help

Commands:
  get [key]                    print a value, e.g. `git.baseBranch`, or
                               everything
  set [options] <key> <value>  set a value in the repo config (or --global for
                               your user)
  help [command]               display help for command
```

## `yuzie config get`

```text
Usage: yuzie config get [options] [key]

print a value, e.g. `git.baseBranch`, or everything

Options:
  -h, --help  show help
```

## `yuzie config set`

```text
Usage: yuzie config set [options] <key> <value>

set a value in the repo config (or --global for your user)

Options:
  --global    write ~/.yuzie/config.json instead
  -h, --help  show help
```

## `yuzie claim`

```text
Usage: yuzie claim [options] <id>

assign to yourself, move to Doing, create and check out the branch (§9.3)

Options:
  --no-branch    claim without touching Git
  --from <base>  branch from this instead of the configured base
  --force        carry uncommitted changes along instead of stopping
  --agent        for agents and scripts: never prompt, stop on uncommitted work
  -h, --help     show help
```

## `yuzie start`

```text
Usage: yuzie start [options] <id>

like claim, but only checks out a branch that already exists

Options:
  --force     carry uncommitted changes along instead of stopping
  -h, --help  show help
```

## `yuzie finish`

```text
Usage: yuzie finish [options] <id>

pre-flight checks, then move the card on for review (§9.4)

Options:
  --skip-checks  move it on without checking
  --push         push the branch first if it is not pushed
  -h, --help     show help
```

## `yuzie branch`

```text
Usage: yuzie branch [options] <id>

print the branch for a card; --create checks it out, --link records one

Options:
  --create       create (or check out) the branch and link it
  --link <name>  record an existing branch as this card’s branch
  -h, --help     show help
```

## `yuzie sync`

```text
Usage: yuzie sync [options]

push queued changes, pull the board, re-scan git, and report what happened

Options:
  --rebuild          clear the cached board first and rebuild it (queued changes
                     are kept)
  --retry-set-aside  put changes the server kept refusing back in the queue
  --drop-set-aside   give up on changes the server kept refusing
  -h, --help         show help
```

```text
Usage: yuzie anchor [options] <id> <location>

  -h, --help  show help
```

## `yuzie open`

```text
Usage: yuzie open [options] <id>

open the card’s code in $EDITOR, or its PR / branch / link in a browser

Options:
  --github    the PR if there is one, else the branch compare view
  --pr        the pull request (falls back to the compare view)
  --browser   the link attached to the card
  -h, --help  show help
```

## `yuzie hooks`

```text
Usage: yuzie hooks [options] [command]

manage the git hooks

Options:
  -h, --help      show help

Commands:
  install         install the hooks listed in git.hooks

```

## `yuzie add`

```text
Usage: yuzie add [options] <title...>

create a card

Options:
  --desc <text>         description
  --assign <handle>     assign someone (repeatable)
  --column <column>     start in this column
  --label <label>       add a label (repeatable)
  --due <date>          due date: friday, tomorrow, +3d, 2026-10-02
  --anchor <file:line>  the code this card is about
  --priority <p>        p0 (highest) to p3
  -h, --help            show help
```

## `yuzie list`

```text
Usage: yuzie list|ls [options]

list cards, most recently active first

Options:
  --status <column>    only this column
  --column <column>    same as --status
  --assignee <handle>  only cards assigned to this person
  --label <label>      only cards with this label
  --mine               only cards assigned to you
  --watching           only cards you watch
  --stale <duration>   unfinished cards idle at least this long, e.g. 2d
  --search <text>      title or description contains
  --limit <n>          at most n cards
  --sort <order>       updated (default), rank, created, due, priority
  -h, --help           show help
```

## `yuzie activity`

```text
Usage: yuzie activity [options]

what happened recently

Options:
  --since <duration>  only this far back, e.g. 2h, 1d
  --card <id>         only this card
  --author <handle>   only what this person did
  --limit <n>         at most n events per page (default 50)
  --before <seq>      the page before this one (the `next` a page printed)
  -h, --help          show help
```

## `yuzie token`

```text
Usage: yuzie token [options] [command]

API tokens for CI, scripts and agents

Options:
  -h, --help               show help

Commands:
  create [options] <name>  create a token; the plaintext is shown once
  list                     your tokens and the ones you issued to agents
  revoke <token>           revoke by id, id prefix or name
  help [command]           display help for command
```

## `yuzie token create`

```text
Usage: yuzie token create [options] <name>

create a token; the plaintext is shown once

Options:
  --role <role>         owner, member or viewer (default member)
  --all-boards          do not scope it to one board (default: this board, or
                        --board)
  --agent <handle>      issue it to an agent, who joins the board as that handle
  --allow-destructive   let the agent delete cards
  --expires <duration>  expire after e.g. 30d or 12h
  -h, --help            show help
```

## `yuzie token list`

```text
Usage: yuzie token list [options]

your tokens and the ones you issued to agents

Options:
  -h, --help  show help
```

## `yuzie token revoke`

```text
Usage: yuzie token revoke [options] <token>

revoke by id, id prefix or name

Options:
  -h, --help  show help
```

## `yuzie completion`

```text
Usage: yuzie completion [options] <shell>

print shell completion for bash, zsh or fish (see `yuzie completion --help`)

Options:
  -h, --help  show help

Install:
  bash  echo 'eval "$(yuzie completion bash)"' >> ~/.bashrc
  zsh   echo 'eval "$(yuzie completion zsh)"' >> ~/.zshrc
  fish  yuzie completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/yuzie.fish

Card numbers and column names are completed from the local cache, offline.
```

## `yuzie upgrade`

```text
Usage: yuzie upgrade [options]

install the latest yuzie, the way this one was installed

Options:
  --dry-run   say what would run, and run nothing
  -h, --help  show help
```

## `yuzie mcp`

```text
Usage: yuzie mcp [options]

serve the board to an AI agent over MCP (stdio)

Options:
  --allow-destructive  let the agent delete cards (its token must allow it too)
  --allow-git          let the agent claim cards, creating and checking out
                       branches
  --audit-log <file>   also append the audit log to this file
  -h, --help           show help
```

## `yuzie feed`

```text
Usage: yuzie feed [options]

stream the board’s events live, one per line (Ctrl-C to stop)

Options:
  -h, --help  show help
```
